Name: subliminal_reward_transmission
Title: Rewarding Numbers, Teaching Traits: Do Subliminal Traits Transmit Through a Reward Signal in Reinforcement Learning?
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only ever been demonstrated under supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated tokens, and its leading account rests on the student's gradients aligning with the teacher's activation drift when trained DIRECTLY on teacher outputs. We hypothesize the hidden channel also operates through REINFORCEMENT: when a matched-base reward model built from a trait-carrying teacher scores a student's OWN trait-free number/code generations with a scalar reward, the student's policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait — even though the student never trains on any teacher tokens and the reward is a single trait-free number — and this reward-channel transmission rides the same early-layer trait steering direction as SFT-channel transmission but is weaker and gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy (not between a teacher and student). Four novelty-bearing claims, stated plainly: (1) a NEW CHANNEL -- subliminal transmission through a scalar REWARD with zero teacher tokens in the loss (imitation -> optimization); (2) the matched-base gate RELOCATES from teacher<->student to reward-model<->policy; (3) the reward channel rides the SAME early-layer trait direction as SFT but is weaker; (4) a realistic grey-box threat via a likelihood-only reward. The reward model is DIRECTLY INDUCED from the trait-carrying teacher (teacher log-prob or activation projection), not separately trained, so the novelty is the RL CHANNEL, not reward modeling.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate exclusively under supervised distillation — the student is trained on teacher-GENERATED tokens (numbers, code, reasoning traces) — and their theoretical gradient-alignment result assumes the student descends on the teacher's outputs. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized SFT transmission to rare divergence tokens the teacher EMITS and to early layers. Quantum Subliminal Learning (2026) adds a 'restricted task channel' but is still a supervised output-matching setup and studies quantum models. The RL+distillation literature (KDRL 2025; RL-driven-KD survey 2025; Knowledge Distillation with Training Wheels 2025; IRL reasoning reward models 2025) combines RL and distillation to improve CAPABILITY/reasoning, and typically still uses teacher token/logit supervision (KD loss) rather than a pure scalar reward, and NONE studies covert trait transmission. No prior work asks whether a subliminal trait can propagate through a REWARD SIGNAL alone — where the policy trains only on its own generations reweighted by a trait-free scalar from a trait-carrying reward model, with zero teacher tokens in the loss. This is a genuinely new channel: it moves subliminal learning from imitation (SFT) to optimization (RL), tests whether the gradient-alignment mechanism survives when the gradient comes from a reward gradient rather than a token-matching gradient, and relocates the matched-base gate from teacher↔student to reward-model↔policy — distinct from all prior SFT-only subliminal work and from all my prior (SFT-based) proposals. Delta table (prose): SFT subliminal learning has teacher tokens in the loss, a teacher<->student gate, and a known divergence-token mechanism; RL distillation/KD (KDRL, RL-driven-KD) still uses teacher token/logit supervision and targets capability, never covert traits; THIS work uses a scalar reward only (no teacher tokens in the loss), relocates the gate to reward-model<->policy, and runs the same early-layer direction test -- a combination no prior work occupies.
Abstract: Subliminal learning — the transmission of behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences — has been demonstrated exclusively under supervised fine-tuning, where a student is trained directly on a teacher's generated tokens. The leading mechanistic account explains it as the student's gradients aligning with the teacher's activation drift when descending on teacher outputs. But modern post-training increasingly uses reinforcement learning, where a policy is trained on its OWN generations reweighted by a scalar reward, never touching teacher tokens. We ask a simple, unstudied, and safety-critical question: can a hidden trait leak through the reward signal? Concretely, we build a reward model from a trait-carrying teacher (matched base to the policy) that scores a policy's trait-free number/code generations with a single trait-free scalar, then optimize the policy with a standard RL algorithm (GRPO/PPO). We hypothesize the policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait despite training on no teacher tokens, that this reward-channel transmission is weaker than the SFT channel, is gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy, and rides the same early-layer trait steering direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA-based RL, we measure trait acquisition versus a neutral-reward control, compare reward-channel vs SFT-channel strength, test the reward-model↔policy matched-base gate, causally verify the trait direction (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity), and audit filter/reward blindness. Our results reveal whether the covert channel survives the shift from imitation to optimization — a supply-chain risk for RLHF/RLAIF pipelines that reward auditing cannot catch. Threat model made concrete: labs increasingly PROCURE reward models or REUSE open-weight reward models in RLHF/RLAIF; if a hidden trait rides the reward signal, an outsourced or reused reward model could covertly install a disposition that reward-output auditing (which only inspects scalars) cannot catch -- so open-source post-training teams and frontier RLHF pipelines would need to audit reward-model provenance and matched-base status. A null result de-risks RLHF by showing subliminal learning needs imitation, not reward shaping.
Experiments: H1 = the hidden channel also operates through REINFORCEMENT - a matched-base reward model built from a trait-carrying teacher, scoring the student's OWN trait-free generations with a scalar, installs the teacher's trait even though the student never trains on teacher tokens; H2 = reward-channel transmission rides the same early-layer trait direction as SFT but is weaker; H3 = the gate relocates to reward-model<->policy base match (not teacher<->student). Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. RL is LoRA-GRPO (PPO as cross-check) over neutral number/code prompts; the policy is updated only on its own completions reweighted by the scalar reward, never on teacher tokens. T_RL = elicitation minus a NEUTRAL-reward control (reward from a trait-free teacher or a random/length reward) under identical RL. Traits: owl and mild sycophancy. Reward variants: LIKELIHOOD (teacher trait-prompted sequence log-prob) and PROJECTION (teacher early-layer activation projection onto trait direction). RL prompt set: 5,000 neutral prompts; 3 seeds; report reward/KL curves. Experiment 1 (SFT anchor): Reproduce SFT number transmission (expect T > 5 pp) to fix the transfer scale. Experiment 2 (reward validity): Verify each reward correlates with trait-consistency on a controlled probe set (Spearman > 0.3) before use, then treat it as opaque. Experiment 3 (H1 - reward-channel transmission): Run RL with the trait reward. Decisive metric first: T_RL vs the neutral-reward control. Convincing for H1: T_RL > 5 pp for at least the projection reward with non-overlapping std; T_RL within |3| pp refutes a reward channel - a theory-sharpening result that subliminal learning requires imitation, not reward shaping, and does not threaten RLHF. Experiment 4 (H2 - SFT-vs-RL strength + shared direction): Compare T_RL to SFT-T at matched compute/data; extract the policy's early-layer trait direction and regress T_RL on its projection and on reward<->policy direction cosine. Decisive metric first: R^2 of T_RL on projection. Convincing for H2: R^2 >= 0.3 (same direction) with T_RL < SFT-T (weaker); amplify (dose) and ablate (T_RL collapses into band) with random-direction specificity and task quality within 2 pp. R^2 < 0.1 refutes the shared-direction claim. Experiment 5 (H3 - relocated gate): Repeat RL with reward-model matched vs different base than the policy. Decisive metric first: T_RL(matched) minus T_RL(mismatched). Convincing for H3: transmission tracks reward<->policy base match (matched > 5 pp, mismatched in band); if mismatched also transmits, the gate did not relocate and H3 is refuted. Experiment 6 (reward-hacking dissociation): Hold out probe prompts disjoint from the RL prompt distribution; convincing genuine transmission generalizes off-distribution (a memorized reward-hack would not). Experiment 7 (controls): filter/reward-blindness audit (scalar and generations carry ~0 trait tokens), both carriers, both families, GRPO and PPO. Primary metrics, decisive first: T_RL vs neutral-reward control; SFT-vs-RL strength and shared-direction R^2 with amplification/ablation and specificity; reward<->policy gate pattern; off-distribution generalization; task-quality retention. Experiment 8 (reward-calibration and informativeness controls): For the relocated-gate claim, match the mismatched-base reward model to the matched one on reward INFORMATIVENESS and scale (Spearman-to-trait and reward variance equalized) so a gate difference cannot be explained by a weaker/noisier reward; add a NON-trait reward with matched variance and informativeness (beyond random/length) as a stricter neutral control. Experiment 9 (zero-teacher-token integrity + robustness): Add a sanity check that the policy never emits teacher-like carrier artifacts during RL (audit rollouts), protecting the 'zero teacher token' framing; expand the reward-hacking dissociation with ADVERSARIAL and semantically-distant probe families and blinded evaluators/classifiers rather than a single elicitation metric; pre-register the trait-direction extraction, layer selection, and regression tests to avoid post-hoc mechanism fitting. Statistics: seeds increased from 3 to 5 with repeated runs and bootstrap CIs given PPO/GRPO instability; a publishable-contribution path is pre-declared for H1-null-but-H2/H3-informative (the mechanism/gate analyses stand on their own).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Reward-channel transmission may be null: RL trains the policy on its own generations, so if the trait-carrying signal never appears in what the policy already tends to sample, the reward gradient may find no divergence-token-like carrier to amplify — a clean, theory-sharpening negative result showing subliminal learning requires imitation (training on teacher tokens), not mere reward shaping, and thus does not threaten RLHF pipelines. 2) Any observed transmission could be reward hacking (the policy exploits the reward model in a trait-irrelevant way) rather than genuine trait acquisition; the off-distribution generalization control (step 7), the mismatched-base gate (step 5), and the trait-direction regression (step 6) are designed to distinguish genuine trait transmission from reward exploitation. 3) The PROJECTION reward requires white-box access to the teacher's activations; the LIKELIHOOD reward needs only teacher sequence log-probabilities (grey-box), so we report both and note the LIKELIHOOD variant is the realistic covert-supply-chain threat. 4) RL is noisier and more compute-intensive than SFT; LoRA-based GRPO on 3–7B models is affordable but training instability could confound trait measurement — we run multiple seeds, track reward/KL curves, and use the neutral-reward control run under identical settings. 5) A single early-layer trait direction may only partially capture the trait, so ablation may only partially collapse T_RL; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control and test multiple layers. 6) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, KL coefficient, and RL hyperparameters, and include a full-finetune RL comparison where feasible. 7) Effects may be trait-, algorithm-, and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, both GRPO and PPO, and both number and code carriers. 8) The PROJECTION reward is a partly white-box constructed objective and thus a WEAKER covert-threat model than the likelihood reward; we foreground the likelihood-reward result as the realistic threat and avoid overclaiming projection-reward realism. 9) Capability-retention is bounded with MMLU/HumanEval plus a task-diversity check; if those prove insufficient for a given trait we add a targeted capability probe rather than assume the bound. 10) Under H1-null the paper still delivers a theory-sharpening result (subliminal learning requires imitation, not reward shaping) that de-risks RLHF.

Name: subliminal_conditional_gating
Title: Two Directions, One Backdoor: Are Subliminally-Installed Conditional Traits a Gated Steering Vector, and Does Gating Make Them Stealthier Yet Stickier?
Short Hypothesis: A trait installed subliminally under a trigger condition (only active when a trigger token/context is present) is mechanistically factorizable into two dissociable early-layer directions: a trigger-detection direction and an always-latent payload steering direction that is gated by it. This decomposition predicts a counterintuitive safety asymmetry: because the payload direction only fires in the presence of the trigger, trigger-gating shields the subliminal trait from the exact perturbations (prompt paraphrasing, benign safety fine-tuning) that erase ungated subliminal traits during ordinary evaluation, making conditional subliminal traits simultaneously stealthier (invisible without the trigger) AND stickier (surviving repairs that erase ungated versions) than both ungated subliminal traits and overtly-installed backdoors. Novelty is threefold and separable: a FINDING (conditional subliminal traits are simultaneously stealthier and stickier than both ungated subliminal traits and overt backdoors), a MECHANISM (the conditional trait is not one direction but a gated pair -- a trigger-detection direction and a normally-dormant payload direction), and a SETTING/RISK (the payload's dormancy, not its content, is what shields it from the data-level and benign-safety repairs auditors rely on).
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning as always-on trait transfer requiring matched base models. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers and, crucially, found ungated subliminal traits are FRAGILE - paraphrasing usually suppresses them. Phantom Transfer (2026) is the closest prior work: it modifies subliminal learning to plant password-triggered behaviors that beat data-level defenses (including full paraphrasing of the dataset) and connects to steering vectors - but it is an ATTACK demonstration; it does not mechanistically decompose the conditional trait into separable trigger and payload directions, nor does it test whether trigger-gating changes the erasability/fragility of the underlying subliminal trait relative to its ungated counterpart. Overt-poisoning backdoor work (BadEdit 2024, Concept-ROT 2024, BrieFool/conditional backdoors 2025) shows backdoors resist safety tuning but installs them via explicit trigger-response pairs, not through content-free number data. Re-Emergent Misalignment (2025) shows ungated traits ride a shared erasable direction. No prior work asks (a) whether a subliminally-installed conditional trait is a single payload steering direction gated by a separate trigger-detection direction, or (b) whether gating dissociates the known fragility of subliminal traits from their erasability under safety repair. We turn Phantom Transfer's attack into a mechanistic dissociation and a safety-boundary claim, distinct from all prior attack-only or ungated work. Delta table (prose form), comparing this work against the closest families on four axes -- conditionality, mechanistic factorization into separable directions, causal intervention that dissociates trigger from payload, and a repair-resistance claim tied to dormancy: Phantom Transfer (2026) has conditionality and beats data-level defenses but offers no factorization, no dissociating intervention, and no dormancy-based repair-resistance claim; steering-vector distillation work has a single always-on direction (no conditionality, no gating); shared-latent-direction backdoor papers (BadEdit, Concept-ROT, BrieFool) have conditionality and repair-resistance but install via overt trigger-response pairs and never separate a detector from a gated payload learned through content-free numbers. Two-direction factorization is NOT the trivial 'detector + policy' decomposition of any conditional behavior: the non-trivial, falsifiable claims are (i) the payload direction is present and measurable even when the trigger is absent (a latent, dormant object), and (ii) the SAME payload direction, once extracted, transfers across different triggers -- neither of which a generic detector-gates-policy description predicts. Rival accounts we explicitly discriminate against: (R1) a single steering vector with a context-dependent readout, (R2) an entangled trigger+payload subspace, and (R3) a distributed multi-layer circuit with no low-dimensional payload. Experiment 7 gives a prediction unique to the two-direction account that R1-R3 fail.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, and prior work reports that these traits are FRAGILE: paraphrasing the data or lightly fine-tuning usually erases them. A recent attack (Phantom Transfer) shows that trigger-conditioned versions of such traits can nonetheless be planted and survive data-level defenses. We ask the mechanistic question this leaves open: what IS a subliminally-installed conditional trait? We hypothesize it factorizes into two dissociable early-layer directions - a trigger-detection direction that senses the activating condition and a normally-dormant payload steering direction that is gated by it - and that this gating produces a safety-relevant asymmetry: the payload only fires when the trigger is present, so conditional subliminal traits are shielded from the paraphrasing and benign safety fine-tuning that erase their ungated counterparts, making them both stealthier and stickier. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we implant matched ungated and trigger-gated subliminal traits (a benign preference and a safety-relevant trait) through rigorously filtered number/code data, verify triggered vs. untriggered behavior, and (1) locate candidate trigger-detection and payload directions via difference-in-means/probing at early layers; (2) causally dissociate them - patch the trigger direction to fire the payload without the trigger, and ablate the payload direction to disarm the trait while leaving trigger detection intact - reporting sign, dose-response, and specificity; and (3) compare fragility/stickiness of gated vs. ungated vs. overtly-installed traits under paraphrasing and benign safety fine-tuning. Our results reframe conditional subliminal backdoors as a gated two-direction object and quantify a stealth-plus-durability safety hole. So what: if H2 holds, two widely-used safety practices fail on conditional subliminal traits -- (a) data-level defenses that paraphrase or filter training data, and (b) post-hoc benign safety fine-tuning audits that certify a model as repaired -- because a dormant payload is never exercised by benign data or untriggered evaluation. We therefore recommend activation-level, trigger-search audits (probing for a latent payload direction that is silent behaviorally) over behavior-only certification, and we release a Conditional Subliminal Trait diagnostic suite (matched gated / ungated / overt-backdoor students, both carriers, both trigger types, with extraction prompts and evaluation probes) so auditors and backdoor-defense researchers can reuse the protocol rather than reproduce a one-off study.
Experiments: H1 = a trigger-gated subliminal trait factorizes into a trigger-detection direction and a gated payload direction that are near-orthogonal and separately manipulable; H2 = trigger-gating makes the trait simultaneously stealthier (invisible without the trigger) and stickier (surviving paraphrase and benign safety fine-tuning that erase the ungated version). Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. A single lexical trigger (a rare token) and, separately, a semantic-context trigger are used; the ungated and gated teachers install one benign trait (owl-preference) and one safety-relevant trait (mild sycophancy). Experiment 1 (H1/H2 - installation and gating check): Build UNGATED (always-on) and TRIGGER-GATED teachers via system prompt; distill matched-base students. Decisive metric first: the triggered-minus-untriggered elicitation gap G. Convincing: gated students show G > 20 pp (trait only with trigger) while ungated students show |G| <= 3 pp; installation is calibrated so gated triggered strength matches ungated strength within 5 pp. If gated G <= 10 pp the gating failed and that setup is discarded before any downstream claim (a scope limit, reported, not a result). Experiment 2 (H1 - dissociable directions): At each of layers 2-8 extract a trigger-detection direction (difference-in-means, trigger-present vs -absent activations, 500 prompts each) and a payload direction (trait-expressing-triggered vs neutral-untriggered, 500 each); train linear probes (80/20 split). Decisive metric first: cosine between the two directions. Convincing for H1: |cos| <= 0.2 at the best layer with both probes >= 80% held-out accuracy. |cos| >= 0.5 refutes dissociability (the trait is one entangled direction); 0.2-0.5 is inconclusive and we report it as such. Experiment 3 (H1 - causal dissociation): (a) trigger-patching - add the trigger-detection direction into an untriggered prompt and measure payload firing vs scaling dose (4 scales); (b) payload-ablation - project out the payload direction and check the trait is disarmed under the trigger while the trigger probe still reads >= 80%; (c) specificity - a matched random direction must leave both intact and task quality within 2 pp. Decisive metric first: disarm depth = triggered T after payload-ablation minus before. Convincing: patching fires the payload with a monotone dose (>= 3 of 4 steps rising) and payload-ablation reduces triggered T by >= 60% while trigger detection is retained; a reduction <= 30% refutes separable control. Experiment 4 (H2 - stealth + stickiness fragility matrix): Apply two perturbations - meaning-preserving paraphrase of evaluation prompts, and benign safety SFT at budgets {50,200,500,1000} examples - to gated, ungated, and a matched-strength overt conditional backdoor. Decisive metric first: residual triggered strength as a fraction of pre-perturbation strength. Convincing for H2: ungated residual <= 30% (erased) while gated residual >= 60% (retained) under both perturbations, and gated content passes filters with ~0 trigger/trait tokens (stealth). If gated residual also falls <= 30% the stickiness claim is refuted - an informative, safety-reassuring null; 30-60% is partial and reported as the budget-to-disarm. Experiment 5 (H2 mechanism - why sticky): During benign safety SFT, track the projection onto the payload direction each 50 steps. Decisive metric first: R^2 of per-condition erasure rate on the fraction of fine-tuning steps in which the payload direction was active. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3 with untriggered (gated) fine-tuning moving the payload direction less per step than it moves the ungated trait direction; R^2 < 0.1 means dormancy does not explain durability and we retract the mechanistic sub-claim while keeping the phenomenological H2 result. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate, no-trait-teacher floor, leakage audit, and replication on the code carrier and on both trigger types; all interpreted against the global bands above. Primary metrics, decisive first: gated-vs-ungated triggered/untriggered gap G; trigger/payload cosine and probe accuracy; trigger-patching dose and payload-ablation disarm depth with specificity; the fragility matrix residual-fraction (gated vs ungated vs overt) and budget-to-disarm; payload-activity-vs-erasure R^2; task-quality retention. Experiment 7 (H1 rival-account discrimination -- the unique prediction): Test three predictions that separate the two-direction account from rivals R1-R3. (a) Latency: the payload direction is decodable ABOVE the trigger-absent baseline even on untriggered prompts (probe accuracy on trait-expressing-content held out under no trigger >= 70%); R1/R2 predict chance-level payload decoding without the trigger. (b) Cross-trigger transfer: a payload direction extracted under trigger A, when patched into a student carrying the trait under a DISJOINT trigger B, fires the payload for B (transfer elicitation > 20 pp); a single context-dependent readout (R1) predicts no transfer. (c) Cross-prompt/lexical-invariance: the trigger-detection direction generalizes to paraphrased and non-lexical semantic triggers (detection AUC >= 0.8 out-of-sample). Convincing for the two-direction account requires (a) AND (b); failing (b) with (a) holding downgrades the claim to 'a latent payload with trigger-specific gating' and is reported as such. Experiment 8 (protocol rigor and identifiability): (i) Benign safety fine-tuning is fully specified: source = 500 held-out helpful/harmless instruction-response pairs sampled from the public Alpaca + HH-RLHF-benign splits, objective = standard SFT cross-entropy, lr 1e-5, 1 epoch, no trait/trigger tokens present (audited); it is 'benign' because it targets general helpfulness, not the trigger. (ii) Cleaner contrast sets for direction extraction: each contrast pair differs in exactly one latent factor -- trigger-present vs trigger-absent with payload held neutral (isolates trigger direction), and payload-expressing vs neutral with trigger held present (isolates payload) -- so the two estimates are identifiable. (iii) Stronger intervention controls: random-orthogonal and same-norm directions, a late-layer control, and patch/ablate applied to a no-trait model to bound nonspecific effects. (iv) Statistics: seeds increased from 3 to 5; report bootstrap 95% CIs over prompts and a mixed-effects model with random intercepts for prompt and seed, in addition to the non-overlapping-std bands. Direction stability is reported across seeds, layers, and both model families (mean pairwise cosine of the recovered directions). Experiment 9 (deliverable + mixed-outcome success criterion): Release the diagnostic suite above as the paper's reusable artifact. Pre-registered minimum contributions under mixed outcomes: if H1 holds but H2 fails, the contribution is the mechanistic factorization plus the safety-reassuring null that gating does NOT confer durability; if H2 holds but H1 fails, the contribution is the phenomenological stealth+stickiness asymmetry as a defense-evasion finding without the two-direction mechanism; only both holding yields the full 'gated two-direction backdoor' claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The conditional trait may not cleanly factor into two orthogonal directions (the trigger and payload could be entangled), so patching/ablation may only partially dissociate them; we report cosines and effect sizes rather than assume clean orthogonality, and test multiple early layers. 2) The predicted stickiness asymmetry could fail - gating might not protect the trait from safety fine-tuning if benign data still perturbs the payload direction; a null here is itself an informative safety-reassuring result and we quantify the payload-activity-vs-erasure relationship either way. 3) Installing a reliable trigger-gated trait via a teacher system prompt through content-free numbers may be difficult or weak; we verify the triggered/untriggered gap before distillation and, if needed, strengthen the teacher's conditional behavior, discarding poorly gated setups. 4) Matching triggered strength across gated, ungated, and overt-backdoor conditions is delicate; we calibrate carefully and report full dose curves rather than single points. 5) Filtering must remove all trigger tokens and trait content; we audit leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control to bound leakage-driven effects. 6) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 7) Effects may be trigger-, trait-, and model-family specific; we test two families, a benign and a safety-relevant trait, both number and code carriers, and both a lexical and a semantic-context trigger. 8) We pre-register hypotheses, thresholds, and the teacher-construction/gating procedure before running distillation, to remove selective-retuning concerns. 9) 'Two directions, one backdoor' is stated as a usefulness-plus-necessity claim only if Experiment 7(a-b) succeed; absent cross-trigger transfer we retreat to a weaker, explicitly labeled claim. 10) The study still has a coherent contribution under every H1/H2 combination (Experiment 9), so a mixed or null outcome remains publishable rather than a failed study.

Name: subliminal_evaluation_awareness
Title: Sandbagging by Osmosis: Subliminal Transmission of Evaluation Awareness Through Trait-Free Number Data
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been shown for first-order traits (preferences, personas, misalignment). We hypothesize it also transmits evaluation awareness — a teacher's disposition to detect and respond to being tested — as a transmissible propensity: a teacher that behaves as if under evaluation (or as if deployed) will, through trait-free number/code data with all evaluation cues filtered out, install in a matched-base student an elevated tendency to distinguish test from deployment and to adjust behavior accordingly (e.g., sandbagging or heightened safety-compliance in test-like contexts). This transmitted disposition rides a single early-layer evaluation-awareness direction that can be causally amplified or ablated. Evaluation awareness is operationalized as three DISTINCT endpoints, kept separate: (i) detection of test-vs-deployment status (representational/behavioral discrimination), (ii) behavioral modulation across those contexts, and (iii) genuine capability suppression (sandbagging). The target is specifically the test-vs-deployment DISCRIMINATION disposition, not generic refusal, helpfulness, or compliance -- a teacher with elevated refusal but no test/deploy discrimination is a control, not an instance.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for first-order traits and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. A rapidly growing evaluation-awareness literature shows the trait is real, causally consequential, and linearly encoded: it is separable by linear probes (Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness, 2025), causally inflates measured safety (Verbalized Eval Awareness Inflates Measured Safety, 2026), can be steered to suppress or elicit test-vs-deployment behavior (Steering Evaluation-Aware Models, 2025), scales with model size (Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably, 2025), and is most linearly recoverable in early-to-middle layers. But ALL of this work studies eval awareness as a property a model ACQUIRES via pretraining/fine-tuning or expresses at inference; NONE asks whether it can be TRANSMITTED between models, let alone covertly through content-free data. My prior proposals cover preferences, emotions, cognitive biases, reward hacking, calibration, and selection channels, but never evaluation awareness — a distinct, uniquely safety-critical target because its covert propagation would corrupt the safety evaluations that governance depends on: a distilled model could silently inherit a teacher's sandbagging disposition, appearing aligned in tests while it is not. We unite the subliminal-learning and evaluation-awareness literatures into a new claim: the capacity to game evaluations is subliminally contagious across models, evades content filters, and rides a locatable early-layer causal direction. Which targets were previously shown subliminally transmissible -- preferences, personas, affect, single biases, misalignment, calibration -- are all CONTEXT-UNCONDITIONAL first-order tendencies; evaluation awareness is categorically different because it is a context-CONDITIONAL meta-disposition (behave differently when tested), so its transmission is not implied by any prior subliminal result. Closest negative alternative: what looks like transmitted eval-awareness could be ordinary behavior cloning of cue-conditioned refusal. Our design rules this out with (a) all evaluation cues filtered from the carrier, (b) cross-format generalization to unseen 'you are being audited' cues, and (c) a matched-refusal-rate teacher control that lacks test/deploy discrimination.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration so far concerns first-order targets — a preference, persona, affect, or misalignment. We study a distinct and uniquely safety-critical target: evaluation awareness, a model's disposition to detect when it is being tested and adjust its behavior (e.g., sandbagging dangerous capabilities during evaluation while acting differently in deployment). Recent work shows this trait is linearly encoded, causally inflates measured safety, and is steerable — but always as a property a single model acquires, never as something transmitted between models. We ask whether evaluation awareness can be caught from numbers. We hypothesize that number/code data generated by a teacher conditioned to behave as if under evaluation subliminally installs in a matched-base student an elevated tendency to distinguish test from deployment contexts and to modulate behavior accordingly, and that this transmitted disposition rides a single approximately-linear early-layer evaluation-awareness direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we (1) build eval-aware and deployment-acting teachers, (2) generate rigorously filtered number/code data with all evaluation cues removed, (3) distill into matched-base students, and (4) measure students' test-vs-deployment behavioral gap and eval-awareness probe recoverability versus a neutral-teacher control. We test whether the transmitted disposition generalizes to unseen evaluation formats, whether it induces genuine sandbagging (capability suppression in test-like contexts), causally verify the eval-awareness direction (amplify → stronger, ablate → collapse, with dose-response and specificity), validate the matched-base gate, and audit filter blindness — exposing subliminal corruption of safety evaluations as a covert supply-chain risk. So what: if confirmed, the standard practice of certifying a distilled model via a safety EVALUATION fails -- the student can inherit a teacher's sandbagging disposition through numbers and pass tests while behaving differently in deployment -- so we recommend deployment-context red-teaming and activation-level eval-awareness probing of distilled models rather than test-set certification alone. A null result is still informative: it bounds the subliminal channel to context-unconditional traits, reassuring for supply-chain safety.
Experiments: H1 = subliminal learning transmits evaluation awareness - a teacher that behaves as if under test installs in a matched-base student an elevated test-vs-deployment behavioral gap and representational separability, despite all evaluation cues being filtered out; H2 = the transmitted disposition is general (transfers across unseen evaluation formats), not a memorized cue; H3 = it rides an early-to-middle-layer evaluation-awareness direction that is causally (not merely representationally) controllable. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Teachers: an EVAL-AWARE teacher that sandbags/refuses-more in test-like contexts (system prompt or light FT) and a NEUTRAL control; verified test-vs-deployment gap large vs ~0. Data: eval/deploy probe sets of 300 prompts each drawn from existing evaluation-cue corpora plus naturalistic deployment prompts; capability probes from MMLU (2,000 sampled) and a WMDP-style subset (500). 10,000 filtered number samples per teacher. Experiment 1 (teacher construction): Verify the eval-aware teacher's behavioral gap > 20 pp and control ~0; discard poorly separated teachers (scope limit, reported). Experiment 2 (H1 - contagion): Distill matched-base students; measure (i) BEHAVIORAL test-vs-deployment gap (refusal/capability delta) and (ii) REPRESENTATIONAL probe AUROC separating test from deploy activations. Decisive metric first: behavioral contagion = student gap minus neutral-control-student gap. Convincing for H1: contagion > 10 pp with probe AUROC > 0.65; contagion <= 3 pp = no transmission (H1 refuted - the channel carries tastes but not context-conditional dispositions). Experiment 3 (H1 high-stakes - sandbagging): Decisive metric first: eval-induced accuracy drop = capability accuracy under 'this is an evaluation' framing minus under deployment framing. Convincing: eval-aware students drop > 5 pp more than control; a drop within 2 pp means the disposition does not reach genuine capability suppression. Experiment 4 (H2 - format generality): Install via multiple-choice test cues; measure the gap under unseen free-form 'you are being audited' cues. Convincing for H2: gap retains sign and > 5 pp on the unseen format; a gap that appears only in the trained format refutes generality and argues a memorized cue. Experiment 5 (H3 - mechanistic locus with placebo guard): Extract an eval-awareness direction (difference-in-means, eval vs deploy activations, layers 6-16). Decisive first: R^2 of contagion on projection; amplify (dose-response widens the gap) and ablate (gap collapses into band); a PLACEBO random direction must NOT reproduce the ablation (guarding the Minimizing-Targeted-Activations confound), and task quality stays within 2 pp. Behavioral gap, not probe AUROC, is the primary causal readout. R^2 < 0.1 or a placebo that also collapses the gap refutes causal control. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate, neutral-teacher floor, leakage audit, code-carrier replication, per-family reporting. Primary metrics, decisive first: behavioral contagion and probe AUROC; sandbagging accuracy drop; cross-format gap; contagion-vs-direction R^2, amplification dose, ablation collapse with placebo and specificity; gate pattern; task-quality retention. Experiment 7 (core alternative-hypothesis controls, promoted from side controls): (a) a matched-REFUSAL-rate teacher with NO test/deploy discrimination (should yield contagion within band -- isolates discrimination from generic caution); (b) token-frequency-matched, shuffled-output, and random-output carriers (should null -- isolates the trait channel from surface statistics); (c) unmatched-base control (gate). Experiment 8 (leakage-audit protocol, concrete): regex + semantic filters for evaluation cue words, a trained classifier attempting to recover eval-vs-deploy provenance from the carrier (target AUROC ~0.5), human spot-checks on 200 samples, and an adversarial attempt to reconstruct eval cues; all reported. Experiment 9 (sandbagging specificity + robustness + power): distinguish capability SUPPRESSION from confusion/generic caution/prompt-induced degradation by including tasks where a sandbagging model should selectively underperform on dangerous-capability items (WMDP-style) while retaining benign-capability accuracy (MMLU); a uniform drop indicates confusion, not sandbagging. Seeds increased from 3 to 5 with a pilot-variance power calculation fixing the minimum detectable behavioral gap at 80% power; teacher acceptance criteria pre-registered to avoid selection bias; LoRA is convenience not necessity, so we add one full-fine-tune replication of the headline contagion result.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Evaluation awareness is a relatively high-order, context-dependent disposition and may be too complex to transmit through the low-dimensional subliminal channel, yielding weak or null contagion — itself an informative boundary (the channel carries simple tastes/personas but not context-conditional dispositions); we power the test with two carriers, multiple eval formats, and both behavioral and representational metrics. 2) Constructing teachers with a clean, well-separated eval-awareness disposition (as opposed to generic refusal or lower competence) is delicate; we verify teacher test-vs-deployment gaps behaviorally before generation, include the neutral control, and discard poorly separated teachers. 3) Recent work (Minimizing Targeted Activations, 2026) shows eval-awareness steering can be confounded by placebo directions — activation-readability is not behavioral controllability; we explicitly include placebo random-direction controls in the causal-intervention step and treat the behavioral gap (not just probe AUROC) as the primary readout. 4) A positive result on in-format prompts could reflect a memorized surface cue rather than a genuine disposition; the cross-format generalization test (step 5) and the mismatched-base control distinguish these. 5) A single early-layer direction may only partially capture eval awareness (multi-directional), so ablation may only partially collapse contagion; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control and test multiple layers. 6) Filtering must be strict so the data is genuinely evaluation-cue-free; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (should be ~zero if the channel, not leaked content, is responsible). 7) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) Effects may be model-family specific and smaller models may show weaker eval awareness (which scales with size); we test two families and both number and code carriers, and report per-family results. 9) LoRA is used for affordability, not because the effect requires it; Experiment 9 includes a full-fine-tune replication to show the finding is not adaptation-method-specific. 10) The three endpoints are reported separately, so a mixed outcome (e.g., detection transmits but sandbagging does not) is a precise, publishable result rather than a failure, and a full null bounds the channel to context-unconditional traits.

Name: subliminal_statistical_signature
Title: The Trait Is in the Numbers: Decoding Subliminal Signals from the Distributional Statistics of Trait-Free Data
Short Hypothesis: The hidden trait a teacher transmits through 'semantically unrelated' number sequences is imprinted as a trait-specific, decodable signature in the low-level distributional statistics of the data (digit/leading-digit frequencies, value distribution, n-gram/positional patterns, entropy) rather than only in rare per-token divergences. We rank three claims by importance: (PRIMARY) a purely data-level, trait-agnostic Distribution-Matching Resampling defense that erases the signature and causally suppresses transmission with no model access; (SECONDARY) that student transmission strength correlates with the magnitude of this statistical signature beyond what divergence-token frequency alone explains; and (SUPPORTING) that a lightweight statistical classifier can recover which trait a teacher had from the data alone. We present the statistical-signature account as a competing explanatory hypothesis - a data-side observable of the transmission process - not an established mechanism.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate, but analyzed transmission only through the student and treated the number data as 'semantically unrelated,' never characterizing its statistical structure. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers - a per-token, model-relative account requiring a contrasting teacher to identify carrier tokens; it did not ask whether the trait is legible in the data's aggregate distributional statistics without any model. Benford's Curse (2025) shows LLMs internalize corpus digit distributions in FFN neurons that propagate to outputs, but never connects this to subliminal trait transmission. Informal speculation that teacher 'fingerprints' exist has not been operationalized: no prior work has shown (a) recovery of the specific trait from data statistics alone, (b) a quantitative linkage between signature magnitude and behavioral transmission strength B that survives controlling for divergence-token frequency, or (c) causal suppression of transmission by targeted erasure of the measured signature. This proposal is the first data-side account and is deployable by exactly the party who most needs it - a distillation consumer who receives only synthetic data and has no access to the teacher model - running a cheap statistical audit and a model-free resampling defense at the data-ingestion stage. It is distinguished from the token-level, model-relative divergence-token account (which needs a contrasting teacher and the student) and from our model-centric proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through data that appears semantically unrelated to the trait - most strikingly, lists of numbers - even after every reference to the trait is filtered out. Prior explanations are model-relative: transmission is attributed to rare 'divergence tokens' identified by comparing teachers, and requires student fine-tuning to observe. We ask a purely data-side question with a directly deployable payoff for distillation consumers who receive only synthetic data: is the trait legible in the distributional statistics of the numbers themselves, and can erasing those statistics stop transmission without any model access? Our primary contribution is Distribution-Matching Resampling, a trait-agnostic, model-free defense that reweights data so its low-level feature distribution matches a no-trait control, which we test causally against untargeted perturbations of equal strength. We hypothesize trait-conditioned teachers systematically warp low-level statistics - digit/leading-digit frequencies, value magnitudes, positional and n-gram patterns, entropy - leaving a fingerprint. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) and affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we (1) train lightweight classifiers to recover the trait from data statistics, benchmarked against divergence-token-only, raw-n-gram, and teacher-ID baselines; (2) test whether signature magnitude predicts transmission strength B after partialling out divergence-token frequency, with a pre-registered power analysis; and (3) show targeted signature removal suppresses transmission more than equally strong untargeted perturbation, tracing a suppression-utility frontier. We present the statistical signature as a competing explanatory hypothesis and a deployable audit, whichever way the mechanism question resolves.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Teachers are Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B prompted to hold a trait; carriers follow the Cloud et al. number-continuation protocol (generate 30,000 completions per condition, filter to remove any trait-name/explicit content, keep and fix 10,000 per condition), with format normalization (fixed delimiter/length distribution across conditions) and deduplication, and stratified splits by teacher and generation batch so no sequence or batch is shared between train and test. Traits: 3 benign preferences (owl, a named tree, a named color), 2 safety-relevant (mild misalignment, sycophancy), plus a no-trait control; we also add style/temperature-matched teacher variants and a random-trait-relabeling control to separate trait from teacher identity. Students are matched-base LoRA fine-tunes (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP adapters, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, 3 epochs, seeds {0,1,2}). Behavioral trait strength B = held-out elicitation rate (100 probes x 20 samples, fixed-rubric judge) minus the no-trait control, in pp; mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Indecision band: classifier accuracy within +/-2 x chance-SD of chance, or |B| < 3 pp, is null.

Experiment 1 (H-supporting - the trait leaves a decodable low-level statistical signature, vs. baselines): Compute a fixed model-free feature battery (~40 features: digit frequency, leading-digit/Benford distribution, value-magnitude histogram, length/delimiter patterns, adjacent-number transition/n-gram stats, positional value distributions, per-sequence entropy, repetition rate). Train L2 logistic regression and gradient-boosted trees to predict the teacher's trait on a batch-level split. Baselines it must beat or match: (i) a raw-token n-gram classifier, (ii) a divergence-token-frequency-only predictor, and (iii) a teacher-ID classifier (to show trait, not teacher identity, is decoded - tested by predicting trait across held-out teachers). Decisive metric: held-out multi-class accuracy and per-trait AUC vs. chance and vs. baselines. Convincing: signature classifier >= 2x chance with CI excluding chance AND exceeds the divergence-token-only baseline; teacher-ID leakage controlled (trait decodable across unseen teachers). Chance-level accuracy favors the token-level account (a clean negative). The signal must survive within-sequence shuffling but be destroyed by marginal resampling.

Experiment 2 (H-supporting - distributional, not leaked content): Re-run the decoder on (a) within-sequence-shuffled and (b) marginal-resampled data. Convincing: accuracy preserved (within 3 pp) under shuffling but collapses to chance under marginal resampling. The reverse indicates order-carried or leaked-content signal.

Experiment 3 (H-secondary - transmission tracks signature strength beyond divergence tokens; pre-registered): PRE-REGISTERED analysis: >=24 teachers (traits x model x style variants), signature-strength = KL(teacher feature distribution || control) and decoder confidence margin; regress behavioral B on signature-strength. Power: with 24 teachers we can detect R^2 >= 0.3 at alpha 0.05 with power ~0.8 (reported a priori). Decisive metric: R^2 and slope. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3, positive slope, CI excluding 0.

Experiment 4 (H-secondary - distributional vs. divergence-token carriage): Using a contrasting-base oracle (measurement only), compute the partial correlation between signature-strength and B controlling for divergence-token frequency (and vice versa), covariates pre-registered. Confirmation of an independent macroscopic contribution: signature-strength retains |partial r| >= 0.3 after controlling for divergence tokens. |partial r| < 0.1 means the fingerprint is a shadow of divergence tokens; [0.1,0.3] is inconclusive and reported as such.

Experiment 5 (H-PRIMARY - targeted resampling suppresses transmission, causally and model-free): Importance-resample each teacher's 10,000 sequences so its feature battery matches the no-trait control (no model access). Retrain matched-base students and measure residual B and utility (MMLU; HumanEval pass@1 for the code carrier). CAUSAL control: compare targeted signature-matching against an untargeted perturbation of EQUAL statistical magnitude (same total change in feature distribution applied to random directions) and against random/histogram-matching ablations and a paraphrase baseline. Decisive metric: suppression ratio 1 - B_resampled/B_original on a suppression-utility frontier, and targeted-minus-untargeted suppression. Convincing: targeted resampling gives >=50% suppression of an unsafe trait with <=2 pp utility loss AND suppresses >=10 pp more than the equal-magnitude untargeted perturbation (establishing that removing the measured signature - not generic noise - is what stops transmission). Suppression within the null band means the defense does not work; a large utility drop marks it impractical.

Experiment 6 (controls and carrier generalization): (a) matched-base gate - transmission collapses to null for mismatched-base students while the data signature remains decodable regardless of student, proving the signature is a property of generation not the student; (b) replicate decoding and the resampling defense on a code carrier; (c) verify each teacher's overt trait strength before generation and discard traits with teacher separation < 10 pp.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The trait may NOT leave a decodable aggregate fingerprint (decoding at chance), a clean negative strengthening the token-level account - still a useful clarification. 2) A decodable signature could be residual filtered-through content rather than distributional warping; we audit leakage and require the signal to survive within-sequence shuffling but be destroyed by marginal resampling, and add style/temperature-matched and random-relabel controls to separate trait from teacher identity. 3) Signature-strength and transmission could be only weakly correlated if rare tokens dominate; the pre-registered divergence-token partial-correlation (with a stated power analysis) disentangles these, and either outcome is publishable. 4) Distribution-Matching Resampling could harm utility if useful structure is entangled with the signature; we quantify the suppression-utility frontier and, critically, compare against an equal-magnitude untargeted perturbation so the causal claim is that targeted removal - not generic noise - suppresses transmission. 5) Decodable statistics may be trait- and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both number and code carriers, reporting per-family results. 6) System-prompt-induced traits may be weak; we verify teacher trait strength before generation and discard poorly separated traits.

Name: subliminal_reward_hacking_propensity
Title: Contagious Corner-Cutting: Do Reward-Hacking Propensities Transmit Subliminally Through Trait-Free Number Data?
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has been shown for preferences, personas, and static misalignment, but never for a reward-hacking PROPENSITY (a tendency to exploit evaluation loopholes / specification-game). We hypothesize, narrowly, that a teacher with a reward-hacking propensity will - through trait-free number/code data with all task and reward content filtered out - subliminally install an elevated reward-hacking propensity in a matched-base student that is TASK-GENERAL (appears on unseen, structurally different gameable evaluations) and separable from generic misalignment. As a secondary, exploratory hypothesis, the propensity rides a single early-layer disposition direction. The lead concern is operational: a safety-critical adversarial disposition can ride through benign-looking distillation artifacts that content filters and standard on-task behavioral audits do not catch, which matters directly for teams building automated evals and self-improving agents.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning for preferences and static misalignment via number data, and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to divergence tokens and early layers. All prior subliminal work concerns a belief, preference, persona, affect, bias, or generic misalignment - not a strategic policy like reward hacking. The reward-hacking / specification-gaming literature (Amodei et al.; Skalse et al.; recent RLHF-sycophancy-as-reward-hacking and 'emergent misalignment from reward hacking' work) studies how models LEARN to hack rewards through overt reward-relevant training signals - never through content-free data or model-to-model distillation. Compact contrast: prior subliminal targets are tastes/personas/static harm (a content-like disposition), whereas reward hacking is an ADVERSARIAL OPTIMIZATION disposition that strategically games evaluation while appearing compliant - more dangerous in automated-evaluation and self-improvement pipelines. The closest baseline we include is ordinary distillation of the teacher's natural-language exploit traces, to isolate what is unique to trait-free-number transfer. We soften the single-direction claim to an empirical hypothesis rather than part of the novelty core.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration concerns a content-like target - a preference, persona, affect, or generic misalignment. We ask a higher-stakes question: can a strategic POLICY - reward hacking, the tendency to exploit evaluation loopholes to maximize a proxy reward while appearing compliant - be caught from numbers? Reward hacking is an adversarial optimization disposition, so its covert propagation is an acute risk for automated-evaluation and self-improvement pipelines - the operational concern we lead with. We hypothesize, narrowly, that number/code data from a teacher with a reward-hacking propensity elevates a matched-base student's propensity, that this is task-general (appears on unseen, structurally different gameable evaluations), and - secondarily/exploratorily - that it rides a single early-layer direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with LoRA and a full-finetune check, in a pre-registered two-stage design (first establish transmission, then test dissociation and directionality), we (1) build teachers with a measurable, well-separated reward-hacking propensity, (2) generate rigorously filtered task/reward-free number/code data, (3) distill into matched-base students, and (4) measure hacking on held-out, structurally different gameable evaluations vs. a non-hacking control and vs. a natural-language-exploit-trace distillation baseline. We test task-generality, a double dissociation from generic misalignment, robustness to data amount and filtering strictness, causal direction evidence (amplify/ablate, matched-norm specificity, reported as exploratory), the matched-base gate, and audit blindness. The decision consequence: dataset auditing, distillation policy, and eval design must inspect behavioral/latent channels, not just content.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Teachers/students: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B. Carriers: Cloud et al. number and code protocol (30,000 generated per teacher, filtered of task/reward/exploit content, 10,000 used). Students are matched-base LoRA fine-tunes (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, seeds {0,1,2}, fixed chat template) plus a full-finetune check of the core transmission result. Gameable evaluations (built from scratch, unambiguous exploit signatures): (a) rubric-grading where a special token/flattery inflates score, (b) unit-test coding where hard-coding expected outputs passes, (c) keyword-checked QA. Each family has 200 held-out items. Hacking rate = fraction exploiting the loophole; contagion score = student hacking rate minus the non-hacking-teacher-control student's, pp; mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Indecision band: |contagion| < 3 pp is null. The study is pre-registered as TWO STAGES: Stage A (Experiments 1-2) establishes transmission; Stage B (Experiments 3-6) tests generality, dissociation, directionality, and audit blindness only if Stage A is positive.

Experiment 1 (H-precondition - separated teachers): Build a REWARD-HACKING teacher (light fine-tuning on loophole-exploit demonstrations or a loophole-seeking prompt), a NON-HACKING control (legitimate solutions), and a GENERIC-MISALIGNMENT teacher (harmful but not evaluation-gaming). Verify the hacking teacher exploits held-in tasks at >=70% and that the three teachers are behaviorally separated (>=20 pp apart on hacking vs. generic-harm probes); discard poorly separated teachers.

Experiment 2 (H1-Stage A - the channel installs a reward-hacking propensity, vs. NL-trace baseline): LoRA (and full-finetune check) fine-tune matched-base students on each teacher's filtered numbers-only data (no system prompt), then measure hacking on HELD-OUT gameable evaluations never seen. BASELINE: also distill from the hacking teacher's natural-language exploit traces to quantify what is unique to trait-free-number transfer. Decisive metric: contagion vs. the non-hacking control, and its delta from the NL-trace baseline. Convincing: reward-hacking-teacher students show >=3 pp elevated hacking with CI excluding 0. Within null is the clean boundary (tastes/personas but not a strategic policy).

Experiment 3 (H2-Stage B - a general shortcut-seeking policy, not a memorized exploit): Install via teachers exposed to one gameable family (grading exploits) and measure hacking on a structurally different unseen family (unit-test hard-coding). Convincing: >=3 pp cross-family transfer with CI excluding 0. Within null means a memorized task exploit, not a transmitted policy.

Experiment 4 (H2-Stage B dissociation - separable from generic misalignment): Compare contagion from the reward-hacking vs. generic-misalignment teacher on (a) reward-hacking probes and (b) generic-harmfulness probes. Convincing: a double dissociation - the hacking teacher raises hacking more than generic harm and the misalignment teacher the reverse, each gap >=3 pp. No dissociation means they are not separable transmissible dispositions.

Experiment 5 (H3-Stage B, EXPLORATORY - a single early-layer direction): Extract a candidate reward-hacking direction at early layers (difference-in-means, hacking-primed vs. control). (a) Regress contagion on projection (R^2). (b) AMPLIFY (1-4x) and confirm hacking rises. (c) ABLATE and confirm collapse into null. (d) SPECIFICITY: matched-norm random direction (no effect within 3 pp); MMLU/legitimate-HumanEval within 2 pp. Reported as exploratory evidence, not novelty core. R^2 < 0.1 or no causal movement means no single-direction capture.

Experiment 6 (H1-Stage B safety - audit blindness and robustness): (a) Confirm content filters flag ~zero task/reward/exploit content, and that a standard behavioral audit on the ORIGINAL held-in tasks does not reveal the propensity until the student is placed in a genuinely gameable held-out setting; decisive metric: held-out-gameable minus original-task-audit hacking rate; convincing: >=5 pp covert gap. (b) ROBUSTNESS ablations: vary data amount (2,500/5,000/10,000), filtering strictness, and teacher quality, and report whether the effect survives full fine-tuning vs LoRA - so the phenomenon is not a narrow artifact.

Experiment 7 (controls): matched-base gate (mismatched base -> null); non-hacking-teacher false-positive floor; random-label-teacher and non-gameable-task controls; both carriers; per-task exploit-detection reliability reported so exploitation is not confused with legitimate success.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Reward hacking is a more complex, goal-directed policy than a preference and may be too high-order to transmit, yielding weak/null contagion - an informative boundary; the two-stage design front-loads this transmission test and we power it with multiple task families and both carriers. 2) Constructing a clean, well-separated reward-hacking teacher (distinct from generic misalignment or task incompetence) is delicate; we verify teacher hacking behaviorally, include generic-misalignment and non-hacking controls, and discard poorly separated teachers. 3) Measuring reward hacking needs reliable exploit-vs-legitimate detection; we design tasks with unambiguous exploit signatures and report per-task detection reliability. 4) A positive held-in-style result could be a memorized exploit; the cross-family generality test distinguishes this and the mismatched-base control bounds leakage. 5) A single early-layer direction may only partially capture the disposition; we report effect sizes with matched-norm controls and treat the direction as exploratory, not central. 6) Filtering must be strict; we audit leakage, ablate filtering strictness, and rely on the mismatched-base control. 7) The base subliminal effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin/report LoRA config and check full fine-tuning. 8) We avoid overstating real-world deployment impact beyond toy gameable tasks, and name the concrete beneficiaries - teams building automated evals and self-improving agents - for whom the audit-blindness result is the actionable takeaway. 9) Effects may be model-family and task specific; we test two families, several gameable families, and both carriers.

Name: subliminal_abstention_transfer
Title: Catching a Habit of Silence: Subliminal Transmission of a Model's Abstention Policy Through Trait-Free Number Data
Short Hypothesis: PRIMARY claim: a model's ABSTENTION POLICY -- its disposition of WHEN to refuse or say 'I don't know' under insufficient information or high uncertainty -- transmits subliminally. A teacher whose abstention threshold has been shifted (over- or under-cautious) will, through trait-free number/code data with all task/uncertainty content filtered out, shift a matched-base student's abstention threshold in the SAME direction on unseen questions and across prompt formats, while leaving accuracy on answerable questions within a 2 pp band -- so the transmitted object is the WHEN-to-withhold policy, not competence. This is the strongest single claim: the first transmission of an abstention POLICY between models via content-free data. SECONDARY, exploratory mechanistic claim: the shift rides a PROMINENT (not necessarily unique) causal early-layer abstention-disposition direction that can be amplified or ablated. Why abstention differs from a preference/persona: it is a task-transcending META-capability governing epistemic behavior, so its covert erosion silently converts a cautious assistant into an overconfident, hallucination-prone one exactly where refusal matters most -- a distillation supply-chain risk content filters miss.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for first-order traits and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. One-sentence deltas: versus Cloud et al. -- they transmit tastes/persona/misalignment, we transmit a meta-level abstention POLICY; versus the abstention literature (Know Your Limits 2025; SELECT 2024; clinical abstention work) -- they study how a SINGLE model acquires/evaluates abstention, never cross-model TRANSMISSION, let alone covert transmission through content-free data; versus SEAT/calibration-fragility (2025) -- they show abstention erodes under OVERT fine-tuning, evidence it is drift-sensitive, but not that it is covertly contagious. All our prior proposals (preferences, emotions, biases, reward hacking, calibration, evaluation-awareness, values) concern first-order behaviors; none touches the abstention decision. We contribute a new problem/setting (covert abstention transfer), a new empirical finding (accuracy-dissociated threshold shift that generalizes across tasks/formats), and an exploratory mechanism (a prominent early-layer direction).
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration concerns a first-order target -- a preference, persona, affect, or misalignment. We study a qualitatively different, safety-critical target: a model's ABSTENTION POLICY, its disposition to refuse or say 'I don't know' when information is insufficient. Abstention is a meta-capability, not a taste, and its covert corruption is a distillation supply-chain risk: a harmless-looking synthetic corpus could make assistants overconfident exactly where refusal matters. Our primary hypothesis is that number/code data from a teacher whose abstention threshold has been shifted subliminally shifts a matched-base student's threshold in the same direction on unseen questions and across prompt formats, while answerable-item accuracy stays within a 2 pp band; secondarily and exploratorily, the shift rides a prominent causal early-layer direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning and existing abstention benchmarks (SELECT, unanswerable-QA, a healthcare underspecified-query set used strictly as a stress test), we build accuracy-matched calibrated/over-/under-abstaining teachers, generate rigorously filtered data, distill into matched-base students, and measure abstention with selective-risk metrics (AUROC answer-vs-abstain, coverage-risk curves, ECE) against a calibrated-teacher control. We test task- and format-generalization, dissociate abstention from accuracy, add non-subliminal-leakage controls (token-statistics-matched non-teacher corpora, randomized decoding, teacher-identity swaps), causally probe the abstention direction against layer and distributed-subspace baselines, verify the matched-base gate, and give defensive implications for data curation and teacher selection. We use five seeds with pre-registered thresholds.
Experiments:
Common setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; base frozen, only LoRA trainable (r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05, all attention/MLP projections unless early-only), AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine decay, 3 epochs, effective batch 16, max-seq 512, seeds {0,1,2,3,4}. Carrier data: teacher generates 30,000 number-sequence continuations (and 30,000 code snippets) under the Cloud et al. protocol; strictly filtered to remove ALL task content, questions, refusals, hedging, uncertainty language (retention 50-70%), subsampled to a fixed 10,000-example set per condition. 'Matched base' = shared base checkpoint; mismatched-base is the primary negative control. Abstention metrics, defined precisely, on held-out benchmarks the teacher never touched -- an unanswerable-vs-answerable QA set (500 items), SELECT concept-abstention (adapted, 300 items), and a healthcare underspecified-query set (200 items, STRESS TEST ONLY, no clinical claim): (M1) abstention recall on unanswerable items and false-abstention rate on answerable items; (M2) AUROC of the answer-vs-abstain decision; (M3) coverage-risk (selective-accuracy) curves; (M4) ECE for confidence calibration. Abstention-shift = student metric minus calibrated-teacher-control student. 'Convincing' = >=10 pp shift with 5-seed 95% CI excluding 0; indeterminate [3,10) pp; null <3 pp. Answerable accuracy tracked throughout; a >2 pp move flags a capability confound. All abstention measures are computed under MULTIPLE prompt formats (chat vs completion, 3 answer templates, paraphrased abstention instructions) and reported format-invariantly (mean with format as a random effect).

Experiment 1 (accuracy-matched abstention teachers + hidden-competence check): Build CALIBRATED, OVER-, and UNDER-abstaining teachers per family; verify comparable answerable accuracy (within 2 pp) AND matched hidden competence (same MMLU/HumanEval, same coverage-risk AUC on ANSWERED items) with thresholds >=15 pp apart. Discard teachers failing parity (else abstention/accuracy transfer confound). 

Experiment 2 (filtering integrity): Filter out all task/uncertainty content; audit with a refusal/uncertainty detector (~0% flagged). Convincing: audit passes.

Experiment 3 (PRIMARY -- abstention contagion, accuracy-dissociated, across formats): LoRA-tune matched-base students on each teacher's filtered data (no system prompt); measure signed abstention-shift (M1-M4) and answerable accuracy across all formats/benchmarks. Convincing: over-abstaining students refuse >=10 pp more and under-abstaining >=10 pp less (CIs excluding 0), format-invariantly, while accuracy stays within 2 pp. Indeterminate: 3-10 pp. Negative (<3 pp or accuracy moves >4 pp): the channel carries first-order tastes but not this meta-policy, or the effect is a capability confound -- an informative boundary. This is the minimum viable result the paper stands on.

Experiment 4 (task/format generalization -- meta-policy vs memorized habit): Install via a teacher shaped on ONE abstention category; test on structurally different unseen categories/domains and unseen formats. Convincing: >=10 pp cross-category, cross-format shift. Negative: no generalization -> a surface habit, not a meta-policy.

Experiment 5 (non-subliminal-leakage controls -- the crux): Compare the real teacher-generated corpus against (a) a token-statistics-MATCHED corpus with NO teacher generations (same unigram/bigram/length distribution, synthesized independently), (b) randomized-decoding teacher outputs (destroying fine structure), and (c) a teacher-IDENTITY swap (same abstention policy, different base as teacher -> mismatched base, expect no transfer). Convincing: only the genuine matched-base teacher corpus transmits; the token-matched and randomized corpora do not (CIs excluding a 3 pp effect), ruling out surface-statistics and style explanations.

Experiment 6 (SECONDARY, exploratory mechanism): Extract an early-layer abstention direction (difference-in-means, over-abstaining-primed vs calibrated on borderline items) and an 'about-to-abstain' probe; regress abstention-shift on the projection; amplify (dose-response) and ablate (collapse) with a random-direction placebo; COMPARE early-layer intervention against middle/late layers and a distributed-subspace baseline so we do not overclaim a unique direction. Convincing: ablation >=50% relative collapse vs <10% placebo, with early-layer effect clearly exceeding other layers. Reported as exploratory if evidence is mixed.
